1. SUMMARY

The BICES Group Executive (BGX), a NATO entity, is the executive body of the BICES Group (BG). The BG exists to enable the sharing and exchange of intelligence and information between and amongst NATO nations, with NATO, and with other non-NATO nations and organisations. Under the leadership of the Director, BGX is composed of the Intelligence and Enterprise Services (IES) Division, the Programme, Engineering and Maintenance (PEM) Division, the Operations and Security Services (OSS) Division, and the Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Cell.

The Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Cell acts as the executive arm of the BICES ISR community. It coordinates the development of an integrated multinational federated ISR Processing, Exploitation and Dissemination capability and enables coherent national, NATO and multinational ISR support to operations by ensuring interoperability, technical and procedural alignment, information flow coherence and collective readiness. The Cell maintains ISR documentation, governance artefacts, interoperability frameworks, reference resources and ISR information required to support participating nations and NATO entities in ISR integration and capability development. It further supports ISR exercises, trials, multinational readiness activities and contributes to long-term ISR evolution.

Under the supervision of the Head, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Cell, and in coordination with the ISR Lead Architect/Engineer, the incumbent administers and provides technical support for ISR services deployed on BICES. As an authorised BGX System Administrator, the incumbent maintains a functional dependency with the BGX Operational Authority and applies approved security and operational requirements when administering ISR systems within the BGX Element and Central Node.

The work is performed in a secure facility where slightly undesirable conditions may apply and involves a light risk of injury. The incumbent participates in the provision of continuous technical support and may be required to undertake on-call and overtime duties outside regular working hours.

Operational travel may be required in accordance with the BG Deployment Policy and national requirements.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

Essential

The incumbent must:

- possess a technical degree or equivalent qualification in information systems management, library science, computer science, information science or a related discipline;

- have at least 6 years of professional experience as a Systems Administrator with background in both Microsoft Windows and Linux platforms;

- have proven experience with the installation, support, configuration and troubleshooting of IT services;

- be able to understand, assess and solve technical issues in a troubleshooting environment under pressure and with time constraints;

- have proven experience with storage, access, problem reporting and change control of Configuration Items (Cls);

- be willing to work outside of normal office working hours;

- possess level V (Advanced) of the English language.

Desirable

The following would be considered an advantage:

- recent experience providing ISR technical services support to military and coalition Operations;

- have proven experience with the installation, support, configuration and troubleshooting of ISR-related services, such as the Coalition Shared Dataserver (CSD);

- experience with ISR service interfaces between STANAG 4559 compliant systems and non-STANAG 4559 compliant ISR systems;

- experience with Information Exchange Gateway solutions supporting ISR service interfaces between different classification level networks;

- experience with status accounting and auditing, in line with recognized standards, such as ISO 9000, 9001 and 9004 throughout the ClS lifecycle;

- certification on Horizon (formerly VMware), version 7 or above;

- certification on IT industry/service provider standards, (e.g. ITIL);

- strong foundation in system security issues;

- French Level II (Elementary).

Expertise Development

Maintain effective technical support for ISR services by assisting nations during capability fielding and testing activities. Provide technical advice and troubleshooting assistance for operational ISR services across approved classified and unclassified environments. Support change and release activities, including testing, rollout and rollback. Participate in Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity testing, record findings and contribute practical recommendations. Maintain current knowledge of technological developments relevant to the assigned work.

Information Management

Maintain accurate and current ISR technical and service documentation and ensure its controlled storage. Review and test ISR-related Standard Operating Procedures to support accurate and consistent application. Collect and report ISR system and service performance data to support service improvement. Provide technical input to reviews of service and support proposals. Support Service Improvement Plans and provide required information to the BGX Configuration Manager. Maintain configuration records for hardware and software installed for ISR functions and services.

Planning and Execution

Administer, operate and maintain assigned ISR systems and services, including STANAG 4559 Edition 4 Coalition Shared Data services, servers, databases, storage, backup and virtualisation environments. Install and configure approved hardware, software and application components in accordance with established procedures. Support testing of national implementations against approved BICES ISR reference tools and record the results. Resolve incidents and customer requests in coordination with the Service Desk, communications technicians, Information Assurance staff and the PEM Division. Provide first-, second- and third-level technical support as required. Implement approved upgrades, changes and modifications to ISR application services, including systems at the Alternate BICES Operations Centre. Monitor system utilisation, capacity and lifecycle status and report identified limitations.

Project Management

Support the timely execution of ISR-related projects and programmes within the assigned technical area. Contribute technical information to project schedules, testing and implementation activities. Coordinate assigned technical actions and report progress, risks, dependencies and deliverables to the responsible manager.

Stakeholder Management

Maintain effective working relationships with appropriate military and civilian officials in participating nations and NATO. Liaise with representatives of relevant scientific and industrial organisations in support of assigned technical activities. Cooperate with BGX Divisions on ISR-related security, event, incident, problem and configuration management activities.

4. INTERRELATIONSHIPS

The incumbent reports to the Head, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Cell. The incumbent coordinates with other BGX staff as required, particularly within the PEM and OSS Divisions, and works cooperatively with ISR Cell technicians.

Direct reports: None

5. COMPETENCIES

Works to meet expected performance standards and deliver outputs within agreed timelines. Applies diligence and accountability in maintaining ISR systems and resolving assigned technical issues.

Analytical Thinking

Breaks down problems and information to identify relationships, patterns and logical conclusions. Applies structured troubleshooting to identify the causes of ISR system and service problems.

Communicates information in a clear and precise manner and checks work carefully for accuracy. Maintains reliable technical documentation, configuration records and test results.

Responds constructively to the needs and requests of internal and external users in support of service quality and mission needs. Provides timely and professional technical support to ISR users and stakeholders.

title: Marine Superintendent
organisation: Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE)
description:
1. POST CONTEXT

This is a position within the Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE), an organization of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
CMRE is an established, world-class scientific research and experimentation facility that organizes and conducts scientific research and technology development, centred on the maritime domain, delivering innovative and field tested Science & Technology (S&T) solutions to address defence and security needs of the Alliance.
As per the STO Charter, CMRE operates under a Customer Funding Regime, whereby customers are charged the direct costs of the services provided plus an overhead to cover general and administrative expenditures, recuperation of capital investments (if applicable) and the Centre operating and running costs. Customers are comprised of NATO bodies, NATO Nations and other parties consistent with NATO policy.
The CMRE consists of four divisions: Research Division (RD), Experimentation and Rapid Adoption (ERA) Division, Engineering and IT Division (EITD) and Operational Support (OS) Division.
The post is located within the Operational Support Division and the Marine Operations Branch (MAROPS) and reports to the Head, MAROPS. The Marine Operations Branch provides safe, effective and compliant operations to CMRE research vessels and coordinates NATO and nations requirements for sea-going programmes of work.
The Marine Superintendent provides professional marine expertise, assurance and operational support to the two NATO-owned research vessels, with particular responsibility for marine safety, regulatory compliance, operational readiness and marine operational standards. The position is hands-on and requires a high degree of professional autonomy, sound judgement and demonstrated ability to deliver practical results. The incumbent works closely with the Ship Operations Manager, Marine Technical Superintendent, Masters and crews.

2. PRINCIPAL DUTIES

The incumbent’s duties are:
Marine Safety, Compliance & Readiness

- Monitor marine safety, statutory and regulatory compliance and the operational readiness of CMRE vessels.

- Provide professional marine advice on operational planning, risk mitigation, safety procedures and SMS implementation.

Onboard Marine Assurance

- Conduct regular hands-on onboard visits, audits, inspections, trials and operational readiness assessments, reporting findings and recommendations to MAROPS management.

- Monitor navigation, bridge practices and onboard marine standards, providing professional advice to Masters and crews.

Emergency Preparedness & Incident Follow-up

- Review emergency preparedness, safety drills and exercises, and monitor relevant corrective actions.

- Contribute to the preparation and review of marine incident and near-miss reports from the marine operational and safety perspective, and follow up agreed corrective and preventive actions. Technical investigations remain under the Marine Technical Superintendent.

Marine Regulatory & Stakeholder Interface

- Provide marine expertise and professional support to the Ship Operations Manager in dealings with Flag State, Classification Society, Port Authorities and other statutory and relevant maritime stakeholders.

- Provide professional advice on applicable marine regulations, statutory requirements and industry standards relevant to marine operations.

3. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND ADDITIONAL DUTIES

a. Flexibility Clause
The incumbent may be required to perform other related duties as directed.
All other related duties should correspond with the required competencies for the job.

b. Deployment/Travel
The incumbent may be required to perform their duties onboard Centre or chartered vessels. The incumbent may be required to undertake TDY assignments within and outside NATO boundaries.

c. Certification
The incumbent needs to hold a fit for sea certificate in line with the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and International Labour Organization (ILO) standards before taking up duty.

4. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

a. Professional Experience

- Relevant professional experience in marine operations, vessel operations, marine safety, statutory compliance, shipboard inspections or vessel supervision, including practical onboard and/or shore-based marine operational experience.

- Valid IMO STCW Certificate of Competency (CoC), at Operational level or higher appropriate to the marine operational responsibilities of the position.

- Demonstrated knowledge of applicable IMO conventions and requirements including STCW, ISM, ISPS, SOLAS, MARPOL and relevant Flag State requirements.

- Practical experience with marine safety, compliance and operational readiness assessment, on-board inspections and/or incident management.

- Demonstrated ability to assess vessel operational condition and compliance, and to identify and follow up appropriate corrective actions.

b. Education

- Bachelor’s degree at a nationally recognised/certified University in Nautical Science, Marine Operations, Maritime Studies or a related discipline and 3 years post-related experience;

or

- Equivalent combinations of relevant education, professional qualifications and at least 5 years practical marine experience may be considered in accordance with applicable NATO recruitment rules.

c. Language Requirements
A thorough knowledge of one of the two NATO languages, both written and spoken, is essential and some knowledge of the other is desirable.
English SLP 3333
NOTE: Most of the work of CMRE is conducted in the English language.

5. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

- Recent or current sea-going experience in commercial, research, survey, offshore support or other marine operations.

- Experience gained as a deck officer or in another operational marine role under an IMO/STCW framework.

- Previous shore-based experience as a Marine Superintendent, Marine Operations Officer, Vessel Superintendent or comparable marine operational role.

- Experience with Flag State authorities, Classification Societies, SMS/ISM, onboard inspections, emergency drills or marine incident investigation.

- Experience in an international and multicultural environment and, preferably, with research, survey or offshore support vessels.

- Knowledge of Italian in order to support marine business with the Host Nation and Flag State is desirable.

6. ATTRIBUTES/COMPETENCIES

The successful candidate possess the following competencies / personal attributes:

- Professional Judgement: Sound judgement in marine safety, compliance, operational readiness and escalation of issues.

- Analytical Thinking: Ability to assess marine operational risks and translate requirements into practical solutions.

- Communication & Stakeholder Management: Clear communication and effective coordination with Masters, crews, colleagues, management and external stakeholders.

- Teamwork: Cooperative approach and ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

- Achieving Objectives & Follow-up: Strong work ethic and ability to deliver results and close agreed actions under operational pressure.

All CMRE personnel are expected to conduct themselves in accordance with the current NATO Code of Conduct agreed by the North Atlantic Council (NAC), and thus display the core values of integrity, impartiality, loyalty, accountability, and professionalism.

7. REMARKS

The duties are performed in an office, laboratory, workshop environment or on-board Centre ships or chartered vessels. Slightly undesirable working conditions may apply. The incumbent is expected to maintain a practical, hands-on approach to marine operations, including regular on-board inspections, trials, drills and interaction with vessel personnel.
__________________________
About Us:
The Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE) is part of the NATO Science and Technology Organization (STO). The mission of the STO is to help position both national and NATO science and technology investments as a strategic enabler and technology advantage for the defence and security posture of NATO Allies and partners. The Centre conducts scientific research and technology development and delivers innovative field-tested S&T solutions to address the defence and security needs of the Alliance. CMRE has more than 60 years of experience and has produced a cadre of leaders in ocean science, modelling and simulation, acoustics and other disciplines, as well as producing critical results and understanding that have been built into the operational concepts of NATO and the Nations.

What we offer:

- Salary (Pay Basis): 4,723.81 (EUR) Monthly*.
*Salary value as per 2026. Subject to future adjustments in accordance with North Atlantic Council decisions.

- Grade ABCL grade B5 / NATO grade G12

title: Network Engineer (LAN & WAN)
description:
For more than 70 years, NATO’s mission has been to preserve peace and security in the Alliance for nearly one billion citizens. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) and its predecessors have worked tirelessly in providing the means that enable the connectedness and togetherness that keep our Alliance strong. We are the NCIA, a team of 3000 civilian and military staff in 29 locations throughout Europe, North America and Asia.

Our technology and cyber experts allow NATO to conduct critical operations, protect NATO’s airspace, make data-driven decisions, defend against cyber-attacks, secure NATO networks and maintain superiority in space. This is all possible because of our greatest force, our people. In order to keep this edge we aim to hire, train and retain the very best staff.

Our staff members represent both the diversity and unity of our Alliance. When you join the NCIA, you will be part of an organization where you can contribute authentically to the mission and purpose of NATO and help us keep our technological edge.

About the job:

Based in Braine L’Alleud* you will join the Agency as we embark on a journey to transform our IT services to support NATO’s Digital Endeavour. You will join the NATO Infrastructure Services Centre (NISC), which is accountable for planning and executing the full lifecycle management activities (design, transition and operations) for the identified area of responsibility. NISC provides generic, domain independent, technical functionality that enables and facilitates the operation and use of Information Technology resources.

* This is a temporary location pending completion of the new SHAPE facility at Camp Casteau in Mons. The Braine L’Alleud site is expected to close by end 2027, with future duty stations shifting to Brussels or Mons, depending on function and business needs.

We are looking for a driven and enthusiastic Network Engineer (LAN & WAN) (internally advertised as Services Engineer) who will take on the following roles and responsibilities:

- Design and implement secure, resilient network infrastructure connecting on-premises and multicloud environments.
- Configure and optimise routers, switches, firewalls and routing protocols, including OSPF, BGP and IS-IS.
- Troubleshoot network faults, latency and congestion to maintain reliable connectivity.
- Apply security controls, assess risks and support investigations into suspected attacks and security breaches.
- Monitor network performance, traffic and capacity to support redundancy, scalability and growth.
- Install, upgrade, patch and remove network hardware and software, testing changes before deployment.
- Collaborate with security, data centre and cloud teams, maintaining clear designs, network diagrams and operational documentation.
- Participate in assigned Enterprise Security Operations Center shifts and scheduled on-call rotations for after-hours support.

For a full list of duties, please review the job description on the NCIA career site.

About you:

The valuable knowledge and experience that you bring to this role are:

- A minimum requirement of a Bachelor’s degree at a nationally recognised/certified University in a related discipline and 2 years post-related experience.
Or exceptionally, the lack of a university degree may be compensated by the demonstration of a candidate’s particular abilities or experience that is/are of interest to NCIA, that is, at least 6 years extensive and progressive expertise in duties related to the function of the post.
- At least 2 years practical experience with the designing, implementing, and maintaining the core network architecture for large organizations.
- Good practical experience configuring, troubleshooting and optimizing routers, switches, firewalls, and other hardware/software networking elements.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills, strong analytical skills and a problem-solving attitude.
- Desirable: Expertise in dynamic routing and traffic engineering, including OSPF, BGP, IS-IS, IPv4/IPv6, MPLS, Segment Routing and QoS.
- Desirable: Experience with SD-WAN, software-defined networking and network virtualisation, plus advanced troubleshooting and automation using Python or Ansible.
- Desirable: Experience in an international military and civilian environment; knowledge of NATO responsibilities and organisation, including ACO and ACT; Cisco or other network manufacturer certifications.
- Fluency in English, both written and spoken

What we offer:

- Genuinely meaningful work as part of the most successful alliance in history;
- 5 year contract with competitive tax-free salary and household and children’s allowances;
- Privileges for expatriate staff including expatriation and education allowances (where appropriate) and additional home leave;
- Excellent private health insurance scheme;
- Generous annual leave of 30 days plus official holidays;
- NATO Pension Scheme;
- Development programs such as professional training, wellbeing, and more

To learn more about NCIA and our work, please visit our website.

The NCIA prides itself on being an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment of mutual respect and value uniqueness and differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnic or cultural origin, age, religion, sexual orientation and physical or neurocognitive ability.

Additional details on the conditions of application can be found via the NCIA career site.

title: Office Head (Travel)
description:
Post Context

Headquarters Allied Joint Force Command Norfolk (JFCNF) provides a resilient, static Joint headquarters to plan, prepare and conduct operations across all domains in peacetime, crisis and conflict, in order to support NATO’s three core tasks, at the Joint Operational level, as directed by SACEUR.

The Finance Directorate (J8) is responsible for all financial management operations and the correct application of all appropriated and non-appropriated funds approved for use by JFCNF.

The Finance and Accounting Branch is responsible for all financial and accounting activities related to international, multi-national credits, NATO Security Investment Programme (NSIP) projects and reimbursable activities.

The Travel Office is responsible for the provision of travel arrangements as well as the overall coordination of transportation services for personnel travelling on official duty provided either by Host Nation or by commercial sources.

Principal Duties:

- Responsible for all aspects of commercial Travel & Mobility for JFC HQ and supported elements.
- Plans, coordinates and supervises the execution of all duty travel in support of JFC HQ and supported elements activities including peacetime operations, exercises and deployments as well as out of region /area operations.
- Manages, plans and directs staff on the day to day management of the section.
- Liaises with the contracted Travel Agency ensuring that optimum service is provided in accordance with agreements.
- Makes decisions regarding the work priorities of the supporting staff to ensure that they match those of the head of the organization and the HQ.
- Plans the routing and itineraries of military and civilian personnel and determine locations, modes and facilities required for the movement of personnel and material by air, rail and surface means.
- Evaluates requests for Special Assignment Airlift missions and coordinates all travel requirements with military entities and commercial agencies to meet target dates.
- Processes all travel order applications, approves, authenticates as appropriate.
- Establishes the most suitable and cost effective mode of travel for each destination.
- Establishes reimbursable rates and, if required, provides information in support of the processing of claims for reimbursement of travel expenses submitted by the traveller.
- Establishes priorities and identifies the most effective method to utilize funds allocated for duty travel.
- Provides travel and cost related information to budget managers of functional areas if directed by Branch Head.
- Provides assistance and guidance to FinS Travel Module users; conducts on the job training and resolves FinS related issues.
- Maintains accurate financial and transactional records relating to HQ travel business.
- Certifies travel-invoices for payment.
- Ensures financial control measures are in place to prevent misuse or abuse.
- Monitors and reports on the performance of the Travel Contractor against the agreed contract. Proposes mitigating actions or process improvements as appropriate.
- Proactively participates in defining, mitigating and managing the risks within the functional area of responsibility in the Finance Directorate/J8 and actively contributes to implement and maintain the internal control framework of the Finance Directorate/J8.

Essential Qualifications / Experience:

- Higher Secondary education and completed higher vocational training leading to a formal technical or professional certification with 3 years function related experience, or Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 5 years post related experience.
- 4 years’ experience and knowledge in the field of commercial travel or transportation management.
- Experience in supervising and managing subordinated staff.
- Experience in office management, billing practices and associated record keeping.
- Experience involving contacts with commercial carriers and transport systems.

Language:

English - SLP 3322 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

Desirable Qualifications / Experience:

- Previous work experience in a NATO, military or International environment and work experience in the field of commercial travel and transportation management.
- Knowledge of the diplomatic, legal and customs regulations affecting travel to/through various countries.
- Familiar with USA & European railway, air and maritime booking systems.
- Experience in funds management, budgeting and accounting.
- Familiar with FinS and all its applications, in order to orchestrate the availability, access and use of the FinS travel module through the JFC HQ.
- FinS Travel Office and Travel FAO courses.

Attributes/Competencies:

Personal Attributes:

- Develops and implements innovative administrative policies and procedures directed at ensuring the highest level of organisational efficiency and productivity. Analyses problems, devises forms and methods to meet changing requirements.
- Acts as subject matter expert in formulating or revising directives and policies for JFC HQ and other NATO HQs. Uses own initiative to determine which course of action is necessary to resolve unexpected problems.
- Sound judgment and initiative are also required to establish priorities and identify the most effective method to utilise funds allocated for duty travel.
- Required to display creative thinking in proposing the adaptation of existing rules or creation of new procedures to comply with new situations such as crisis operations and out-of-area operations.
- Experience must enable the incumbent to undertake work in which considerable independence of thought and actions are required.
- Good health, stress tolerance and ability to work long hours when required. Must be capable of working in a demanding environment and have the necessary tact and personality to be able to work with staff, both military and civilian, at all levels and of different nationalities.

Managerial Responsibilities:

- Responsible for the planning of the day to day management of the section and directs the staff (one military workforce) accordingly.

Professional Contacts:

- The position involves professional contacts with managerial counterparts in NATO and outside immediate organisation with commercial carriers and various providers. Due to the nature of this post, the incumbent has frequent internal and external high-level contact including co-ordination and negotiation with senior civilians and military typically at OF4/ OF5 level, with whom discussions involve obligating resources of the organization and/ or formulation of policies take place.

Contribution To Objectives:

- Responsible for a crucial logistics support function, ensuring that operational requirements and target dates are met by coordinating transportation requirements with military and commercial agencies. The provision and procurement of travel services is not a purchasing activity, but a complex logistics support function, which falls directly under the responsibility of the incumbent.
- The incumbent's performance, guidance and knowledge have a significant financial impact on the JF HQ budget for travel. In addition to ensuring financial controls and protections are in place to avoid misuse or abuse, the incumbent is involved in many exceptional needs that arise. Ensuring that such needs, particularly those that have operational significance, are properly met, is an important part of the responsibilities of this post.
- The successful management of financial resources is considered vital to the achievement of the objectives and mission of the HQ. The incumbent contributes to mission objectives by establishing, monitoring and improving the travel process, in monitoring and simplifying internal procedures and in carrying out cost effective commitments. The incumbent's performance has a material impact on the travel budget and as such is critical to maintaining JF HQ and NATO's military capabilities.

Security Clearance

The successful applicant will be required to apply for and receive a NATO Secret Security Clearance prior to final confirmation of contract and commencement of employment.

The incumbent may be required to undertake deployments in support of military operations and exercises, and/or TDY assignments, both within and without NATO boundaries. Such operational deployment may exceed 30 days duration up to 183 days in any period of 547 days and may be on short notice. For NATO International Civilian staff, acceptance of an employment contract linked to this post constitutes agreement to deploy in excess of 30 days if required.

Contract

Serving NATO International Civilian staff will be offered a contract in accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations. Newly recruited staff will be offered a three year definite duration contract.

1. SUMMARY

The Political Affairs and Security Policy (PASP) Division leads on the political aspects of NATO’s core tasks and is the International Staff’s (IS) political hub for partnerships. To enable PASP to deliver on its partnership responsibilities, a number of NASOs around the globe has been established to provide an in-situ interface with the respective partner countries/international organisations.
Within the Divisional Support Section (DSS), and working closely with multiple relevant stakeholders across NATO HQ, the Officer acts as the focal point in PASP for NASO heads to ensure the effective functioning of the NASOs for the budget, human resources (HR), security and safety, host nation legal arrangements, logistics, ICT and business continuity domains. The incumbent of the post will be expected to visit the NASOs periodically, which may include travel to non-permissive environments. The incumbent will deputize for the Executive Officer/Head DSS, in cases of absence, when necessary.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The incumbent must:
• possess a university degree, or an equivalent level of qualification in a relevant field;
• have at least 3 years’ relevant experience in progressively responsible positions with a focus on policy, budget, administration and/or HR;
• have experience in project management and working with a large stakeholder group on a diverse range of topics;
• possess the following minimum levels of NATO’s official languages (English/French): V (“Advanced”) in one and II (“Elementary”) in the other.

The following would be considered an advantage:
• excellent knowledge of NATO HQ’s organisation, procedures and practices;
• an overall understanding of Euro-Atlantic security issues and the contribution of partnerships to NATO’s cooperative security;
• experience coordinating activities and/or operations across multiple offices or entities within governmental, intergovernmental, international, or other institutional environments.

3. MAIN ACCOUNTABILITIES

Project Management. Lead on NASO coordination within PASP, with other Divisions and between the International Staff (IS) and the International Military Staff (IMS). Monitor compliance with all tasks issued by the Office of the Secretary General (OSG) and the Assistant Secretary General (ASG) PASP in relation to NASOs. Plan, organise and support projects, as relevant to enable the functioning of NASOs. This may include, inter alia, security and safety upgrades; the establishment or refurbishment of premises; the deployment of IT and communications capabilities; staffing related matters; fleet requirements; and business continuity planning.

Information Management. Follow-up and report on the NASOs’ internal management issues, exchanging information as appropriate. Facilitate information-sharing across HQ-based stakeholders with a view to ensure a fluent exchange of knowledge between the NASOs and HQ counterparts.

Expertise Development. Assist and advise PASP’s senior management in all matters pertaining to support to the NASOs. Ensure the consistent application of the NASO Handbook and initiate and contribute to its regular review and revision, as required. Draft position papers and conduct analyses as necessary in coordination with other Divisions/IOs. Synthesize information from a variety of sources, develop conclusions and present results to senior level management in a clear and concise manner.

Stakeholder Management. Serve as the PASP internal and external point of contact for all matters relating to NASO support. Maintain close collaboration with heads of Satellite Offices and local staff in support to their operations and particular activities. Lead the secretariat support to the NASO Support Working Group (NSWG), including timely preparation and circulation of meeting agendas and supporting documentation, and follow on actions.

4. INTERRELATIONSHIPS

Reporting Line: The incumbent reports to the Executive Officer/Head Divisional Support Section.
Interactions: The incumbent works closely with the Budget Officer, Directors and Section Heads in PASP on identifying and discussing current needs and likely future developments regarding the NASOs. title: Officer, Partnerships
description:
1. Post Context.

The mission of the NATO Science & Technology Organization (STO) is to help position the Nations and NATO’s S&T investments as a strategic enabler of the knowledge and technical advantage for the defence and security posture of NATO and Partner Nations.
The Office of the Chief Scientist (OCS) is chartered to provide executive and administrative support to the Chief Scientist in fulfilling his/her roles as the Chair of the STB and the senior scientific advisor at NATO Headquarters.
The Strategy & Policy Branch (GSX) provides the primary support to the Chief Scientist in policy development and the implementation of policies and programmes. The Branch drafts and develops the STB guidance for the STO, the NATO S&T Enterprise and the wider S&T ecosystem, and oversees its implementation. Furthermore, SPO performs strategic outreach to NATO S&T Enterprise and ecosystem, promotes STO partnerships, and prepares strategic messages for the Chief Scientist at STO corporate level.

Candidates are requested to provide a motivation letter outlining their interest in the position and relevant experience. The motivation letter will be taken into consideration as part of the selection process.

2. Principal Duties.

The Officer, Partnership supports the Chief Scientist by managing the STO’s institutional and political partnerships, and developing plans and engagements in line with STO strategic objectives. The incumbent is responsible for:

a. Managing and developing STO institutional partnerships (with other NATO entities, and other organisations such as the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, the NATO Innovation Fund, and the NATO-accredited Centres of Excellence) by:

• Maintaining oversight over STO Partnerships with other entities;
• Developing new and revising existing partnership agreements, as directed by the Chief Scientist and in close coordination with the Head, Strategy and Policy;
• Coordinating the implementation of STO institutional partnerships across STO and with the respective institutional partner, e.g., through annual action plans (as defined in the specific partnership agreements agreed by the STB);

b. Managing and developing STO political partnerships (with non-NATO countries), in accordance with extant NATO partnership policies, by:

• Maintaining oversight over NATO’s Individually Tailored Partnership Programmes (ITPP), in particular the S&T elements therein;
• Draft STO contributions to ITPPs, and coordinate those drafts within the STO and with NATO HQ staffs;
• Engage with Partner country representatives on ITPPs.

c. Maintaining an overview of NATO partnership policies relevant to STO;

d. Supporting the Head, Strategy & Policy by:

• Advising on updates and revisions of STO partnership policies;
• Formulating recommendations and promoting new organisational schemes of cooperation aimed at institutionalising partnerships.

e. Acting as principal PoC for all partnership-related questions, both internal to the STO (from STB, STCs, CSO, CMRE) and external to the STO (in particular from IS/PASP and IMS/CS);

f. Contributing to the development and implementation of the STB priorities, including the NATO S&T Strategies and NATO S&T Priorities, as well as STB initiatives and policies.

3. Special Requirements and Additional Duties.

• Performing other related functions, as directed by the Chief Scientist.
• The functions involve irregular working hours and frequent travel abroad, including on weekends.

a. Professional/Experience.

The incumbent must have:
• Broad knowledge of research and development organisations.
• Broad knowledge of programmes and activities within NATO member states’ S&T communities.
• Broad operational knowledge of military technology.
• A significant previous experience, minimum 3 years, of working in a Science & Technology environment at different management levels.
• 3-year experience in working in an international environment having demonstrated the capability of working in a multinational and multicultural environment with scientific and military personnel at all levels. This pertains in particular to NATO or comparable organizations.
• Proven skills in authorship of clear and concise documents; and giving effective presentations.
• Sufficient managerial experience in the same or related career field at various levels of responsibility.
• Working knowledge of office word processing, spreadsheet, graphics presentations and database software.

b. Education/Training.
• A degree from a university or institute of recognised standing or an equivalent qualification from a defence/military institution, for example in a scientific, technical, engineering or mathematical discipline.

c. Language Requirements.
• Very good knowledge of one of the two official NATO languages, English or French (SLP 4444), good knowledge of the other (SLP 3333). The work is mainly conducted in the English language.

5. Desirable Qualifications.

a. Professional/Experience.

The incumbent should have:
• Experience in a Ministry or Department of Defence dealing with the development of defence capabilities and military technology.
• Practical management experience in planning, programming and budgeting.
• Proven skills in leadership, conflict resolution and negotiating, chairing meetings, and training of subordinates.
• Experience in supervising staff.

b. Education/Training.
• A state or university post-graduate degree in a scientific, technical, engineering or mathematical discipline of interest to defence and/or security.

c. Language Requirements.
• Knowledge of other languages.

• Initiative.
• Analytical thinking.
• Tact and capacity to co-operate and work harmoniously with high-level civilian and military personnel of different NATO Nations.
• Reliability.
• Trustworthiness, discretion and high sense of responsibility.

title: Principal Technician (ICT Systems)
description:
Who we are:

For more than 70 years, NATO’s mission has been to preserve peace and security in the Alliance for nearly one billion citizens. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) and its predecessors have worked tirelessly in providing the means that enable the connectedness and togetherness that keep our Alliance strong. We are the NCIA, a team of 3000 civilian and military staff in 29 locations throughout Europe, North America and Asia.

Our technology and cyber experts allow NATO to conduct critical operations, protect NATO’s airspace, make data-driven decisions, defend against cyber-attacks, secure NATO networks and maintain superiority in space. This is all possible because of our greatest force, our people. In order to keep this edge we aim to hire, train and retain the very best staff.

Our staff members represent both the diversity and unity of our Alliance. When you join the NCIA, you will be part of an organization where you can contribute authentically to the mission and purpose of NATO and help us keep our technological edge.

About the job:

Based in Northwood, The UK, you will join the Agency as we embark on a journey to transform our IT services to support NATO’s Digital Endeavour. You will join CSU Northwood, located in Northwood, The UK, is responsible to manage, deliver and maintain assigned Communication and Information Systems (CIS) products and services for the Agency’s customers during peacetime, crisis and war throughout its assigned AoR and as otherwise directed. As the local service provider and Service Management Authority (SMA), it supports the NCIA in delivering secure, reliable end-to-end services under the Enterprise Service Delivery Model (ESDM).

We are looking for a driven and enthusiastic Principal Technician (ICT Systems), who will take on the following roles and responsibilities:

- Assists in designing, verifying, documenting, amending and refactoring moderately complex software configurations for deployment.

- Applies agreed standards and tools, to achieve a well-engineered result.

- Monitors operational systems for resource usage and failure rates, to inform and facilitate system software tuning.

- Applies system software parameters to maximise throughput and efficiency.

- Carries out agreed network maintenance tasks and specified operational configuration of network components.

- Establish and diagnose network problems/faults using the required troubleshooting methodology and tools.

- Installs or removes hardware and/or software, using supplied installation instructions and tools, including handover to the client.

- Uses standard procedures and diagnostic tools to test installations, correct problems, and document results.

For a full list of duties, please review the job description on the NCIA career site.

About you:

The valuable knowledge and experience that you bring to this role are:

- Higher vocational training in a relevant discipline with 3 years post-related experience. Or a secondary educational qualification with 5 years post-related experience.

- At least 3 years practical experience of implementation and maintenance of ICT end systems within a large organization.

- Good experience configuring hardware and software.

- Good understanding of ICT systems and the ability to work independently to solve problems.

- Hands-on experience troubleshooting technical issues and providing technical support to end-users.

- Fluency in English, both written and spoken.

What we offer:

- Genuinely meaningful work as part of the most successful alliance in history;

- 5 year contract with competitive tax-free salary and household and children’s allowances;

- Privileges for expatriate staff including expatriation and education allowances (where appropriate) and additional home leave;

- Excellent private health insurance scheme;

- Generous annual leave of 30 days plus official holidays;

- NATO Pension Scheme;

- Development programs such as professional training, wellbeing, and more.

To learn more about NCIA and our work, please visit our website.

The NCIA prides itself on being an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment of mutual respect and value uniqueness and differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnic or cultural origin, age, religion, sexual orientation and physical or neurocognitive ability.

Additional details on the conditions of application can be found via the NCIA career site.

Undertakes all additional duties as directed by Director POSH.

- Knowledge of Organizational Change Management.

- French - SLP 2222 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

Training :

- Microsoft Project

- ISO 19650 - Organization and digitization of information about buildings and civil engineering works, including building information modelling (BIM) — Information management using building information modelling

- Automation design software

- Change Management

- Discretion, good inter personal skills , tact and diplomacy, and excellent communication skills are predominant in negotiation with key stakeholders’ at leadership level to represent SHAPE’s position affecting the realization of strategic objectives and benefits

- Strong analytical thinking, pro-active problem-solving, initiative and creative thinking, particularly in areas where there are no clear models/precedents to guide.

- Clarity of thought, sound consistent judgment combined with strong technical knowledge, and lateral thinking are indispensable for the development of new concepts, techniques and procedures to bridge the challenge of the diverse application of varying national engineering stanndards and practices which, in addition, may have possible inherent political ramifications and sensitivities.

title: Staff Assistant (Civilian Personnel)
description:
ABOUT YOU

We are looking for a motivated professional to join our Human Resources Management Division as Staff Assistant (Civilian Personnel). For this role, you will contribute to the efficient execution of all aspects of personnel administration for NATO international civilian (NIC) personnel and advise staff and management. Your key focus will be:

- Contracts of Employment for NATO international civilian personnel

- Employee Performance Management

THE ROLE

In particular, you will be responsible for:

- Modernizing onboarding processes by implementing automated processes and optimizing procedures to streamline new-hire integration and enhance engagement;

- Participating in the digitization and automation of employee lifecycle processes to reduce manual effort, enhance operational efficiency, and ensure accurate data management across Human Resources (HR) systems;

- Implementing Human Resources programmes, including staffing, employment processing, health and welfare benefits, training, records and performance management, safety, succession planning, employee relations, retention, deployments, and personnel transactions;

- Assisting in developing HR solutions and improving manager and employee performance by identifying and resolving issues, providing coaching and counselling, and ensuring compliance with the performance management system;

- Reviewing staff complaints or grievances related to performance and initiating actions to resolve them;

- Assisting in the completion of special projects;

- Assisting in preparing reports, papers, and briefings by collecting, analysing, and summarising data and trends, and supporting special projects;

- Ensuring compliance with international and national legal requirements by studying, anticipating, and enforcing legislation, and advising management on necessary actions;

- Assisting in planning, drafting, and implementing operational plans, policies, and procedures for NATO civilian deployments, providing expert advice on deployment issues and coordinating pre-deployment preparation, training, and out-processing of NATO civilian staff.

YOUR PROFESSIONAL/EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND

Essential Qualifications

- Higher Secondary education and intermediate vocational training in human resources management, business administration, law, social sciences, or related field, public administration or related discipline which might lead to a formal qualification with 2 years’ experience,

OR Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

- Experience in Staff Acquisition, Performance Management, Training Management, Maintaining Employees Files, People skills, Resolving Conflict, Employment Law, Project Management, Reporting Skills, Verbal Communication, Administrative Writing Skills and Employee Relations Management.

- Experience in personnel administration and personnel management.

- Professional experience in office/general administration practices.

- Experience in application of Personnel Regulations.

- Experience in Employee Performance Management.

- In-depth working knowledge of MS Office Word, and practical knowledge for Excel, Power Point, SharePoint and Outlook programs.

- The work both oral and written, in this post and in this Headquarters as a whole, is conducted mainly in English therefore sufficient English proficiency is essential.

Desirable qualifications:

- Experience in an international organization or military environment.

- German language proficiency.

YOUR SKILLS

Time Management: Judgment in prioritizing responsibilities and planning and organizing own tasks to keep suspenses.

Initiative: Own initiative, recommending improvements in office administration policies and procedures.

Discretion: Integrity, discretion and interpersonal sensitivity are called for, as private and personal information is handled.

Teamwork: Strong teamwork skills, working well with others and helping a group reach a common goal.

Innovation: The creation, implementation, or introduction of new ideas or methods that add value and bring about effective change.

WHY TO WORK FOR US?

By joining our organization, you will be part of a multi-national team while working towards NATO`s common goal of safeguarding peace and promoting democratic values for over a billion people. We are committed to fostering a collaborative work environment built on mutual respect and professionalism, where every individual’s work makes a difference and has a meaningful impact on the mission and operation of the Alliance. If this resonates with you, we encourage you to apply.

YOUR TEAM

The Human Resources Management Division is responsible for the provision of consistent, effective, and efficient workforce planning, civilian and military personnel management, talent management, including the management of staff training. The Division manages the Central Processing Centre of the Force.

The Civilian Personnel Branch (CPB) is responsible for full spectrum of civilian HR management activities as required and manages the deployment of civilian staff.

The Civilian Personnel Administration Section is responsible for the complete personnel administration, including payroll and budget administration, for all NATO international civilian personnel.

HOW TO APPLY

· Co-ordinate routine Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable and Travel commitment documents, for propriety, completeness and for budgetary authority and availability.

· To the extent delegated by the Branch Head, authorize commitment of funds along with increases and decreases to existing commitments as required.

· Monitor and prioritize tasks to ensure all suspense dates are met on time.

· Ensure that commitments are charged to the proper budget account and that sufficient funds are available.

· Oversee authorization and processing of advances.

· Co-ordinate routine fiscal/accounting matters with team and other staff elements within headquarters, and national agencies.

· Assist with the maintenance of computerized financial accounts and the preparation of related reports, checklists, management accounts and year-end procedures.

· Organize own workload to ensure accurate and timely execution of duties.

· Control commitments and ensure that required receipts and other supporting documentation are attached to all financial transactions.

· Review invoices and verify the legitimacy in respect of NATO and national rules, unit prices and mathematical accuracy.

· Manage filling of all source documents to include travel, accounts payable and accounts receivable.

title: Staff Officer (Exercises)
description:
Who we are:

For more than 70 years, NATO’s mission has been to preserve peace and security in the Alliance for nearly one billion citizens. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) and its predecessors have worked tirelessly in providing the means that enable the connectedness and togetherness that keep our Alliance strong. We are the NCIA, a team of 3000 civilian and military staff in 29 locations throughout Europe, North America and Asia.

Our technology and cyber experts allow NATO to conduct critical operations, protect NATO’s airspace, make data-driven decisions, defend against cyber-attacks, secure NATO networks and maintain superiority in space. This is all possible because of our greatest force, our people. In order to keep this edge we aim to hire, train and retain the very best staff.

Our staff members represent both the diversity and unity of our Alliance. When you join the NCIA, you will be part of an organization where you can contribute authentically to the mission and purpose of NATO and help us keep our technological edge.

About the job:

Based in Mons, Belgium you will join the Agency as we embark on a journey to transform our IT services to support NATO’s Digital Endeavour. You will join the Chief Service Operation (CSO) that is accountable to plan, operate and maintain CIS services throughout the allocated Area of Responsibility. Moreover, CSO serves as signature authority for Agency orders involving deployment of staff and equipment to Operations and Exercises and is responsible for CIS operational situational awareness to the General Manager (GM) and Chief of Staff (COS) as well as exercises coordination authority for day-to-day in-service support across the Agency's portfolio.

We are looking for a driven and enthusiastic Staff Officer (Exercises) who will take on the following roles and responsibilities:

· When tasked, represents NCIA in the Military Training Exercise Programme (MTEP) process, and acts as the NCIA central point of contact for SHAPE J7

· Participate in Exercise planning and coordination activities according to agreed Agency support

· Assumes the role of NCIA Officer Primary Responsible (OPR) in charge of coordinating the preparation, execution and analysis of exercises, both internally within NCIA and with external stakeholders (notably the CIS OPR of the exercise), unless assigned to another OE (mainly for local exercises; in this case, OE reports to OPEX Centre to ensure overall supervision of the exercises supported by NCIA).

Acts as Project Manager (PM) for those elements of support to exercises that are covered by a project initiated by a CR or equivalent i.e. above existing CIS support arrangements, unless assigned to another OE

For a full list of duties, please review the job description on the NCIA career site.

About you:

The valuable knowledge and experience that you bring to this role are:

· A minimum requirement of a Bachelor's degree at a nationally recognized/certified University in a related discipline, mainly in CIS/ICT domain and 2-years post-related experience. Or, exceptionally, the lack of a university degree may be compensated by the demonstration of a candidate's particular abilities or experience that is/are of interest to NCIA, that is, at least 6-years extensive and progressive expertise in duties related to the function of the post.

· Staff Officer with CIS experience in a National or International HQ at divisional level or above are required

· Broad knowledge of planning/executing Exercises

· Experience with team management and training personnel

· Fluency in English, both written and spoken

What we offer:

· Genuinely meaningful work as part of the most successful alliance in history;

· 5 year contract with competitive tax-free salary and household and children’s allowances;

· Privileges for expatriate staff including expatriation and education allowances (where appropriate) and additional home leave;

· Excellent private health insurance scheme;

· Generous annual leave of 30 days plus official holidays;

· NATO Pension Scheme;

· Development programs such as professional training, wellbeing, and more

To learn more about NCIA and our work, please visit our website.

The NCIA prides itself on being an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment of mutual respect and value uniqueness and differences in gender, gender identity, race, ethnic or cultural origin, age, religion, sexual orientation and physical or neurocognitive ability.

Additional details on the conditions of application can be found via the NCIA career site.

title: Staff Officer (Industrial Security)
description:
Job Title: Staff Officer (Industrial Security)

Description

The Joint Warfare Centre (JWC) is seeking an Industrial Security professional to join its Security Section within the Support Directorate. The role supports the implementation of NATO security policies and procedures, with a focus on protecting NATO classified information handled by industry in the context of contracts. The position contributes to ensuring that classified information generated, shared, or managed under industrial contracts is safeguarded in accordance with NATO Security Policy and supporting directives.

What we offer:

Ø A meaningful role supporting NATO’s mission and readiness

Ø Work in a professional, international environment

Ø A key role in protecting classified information in industry contracts

Ø Exposure to NATO security policy and industrial security procedures

Ø Direct contribution to NATO training, exercises, and resilience

If you bring your expertise in industrial security, classified contracts management, and policy development, we encourage you to apply.

NATO Body: Joint Warfare Centre (JWC)

Primary Location: Stavanger, Norway

Schedule: Full-Time

Salary (Pay Basis): 93,933.00 NOK Monthly

Grade: G15

Clearance Level: NATO Secret (NS)

Application Deadline: 25 October 2026

Please note that the JWC is currently trialling a new organizational structure. Consequently, reporting lines, job titles, functional alignments and some duties may differ slightly from those outlined in this vacancy notice

Duties

Ø To ensure the application of protective measures and procedures to prevent, detect and recover the loss of compromise of classified information handled by industry in contracts.

Ø To ensure that before a facility, contractor, industry partner or other non-NATO entity can have access to NATO Classified Information (NCI), that they have been correctly checked for the ability to protect and use NCI in an appropriate manner to ensure its integrity.

Ø To be the conduit between the JWC Security Office, industry partners, and all applicable National Security Authorities (NSAs), facilitating personnel and project security requirements.

Ø To provide assurance that all Industry Partners possess the appropriate NATO security clearance level and have been approved by the North Atlantic Council (NAC) to share and receive NCI.

Ø To Lead the management and development of Classified Project and Industrial Security procedures, involving engagement with NATO HQ, NSAs, JWC Project Officers and key stakeholders.

Ø To ensure the application of NATO Personnel Security policy, supporting directives, and instructions, elevating risks and issues in accordance with JWC Operating Instructions and Procedures.

Ø To manage and maintain a personnel security database for all industry partners who are granted access to NCI and NATO Class II security areas by the JWC.

Ø To assist the JWC Security Office with general administrative tasks related to all security domains and support security operations related to exercises and events hosted at the JWC.

Ø Investigates minor security breaches in accordance with established procedures.

Ø Assists users in defining their access rights and privileges.

Ø Performs non-standard security administration tasks and resolves security administration issues.

Qualifications

Education/Training

Ø University Degree in security administration, criminology, public administration, industrial security administration, law, contract management, procurement, accounting or related discipline,

Ø or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training in that discipline leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation

Professional Experience

Ø 4 years of experience in Industrial security and classified contracts management

Ø 4 years of experience in business or office administration

Ø 2 years of experience in security policy development

Ø 2 years of experience in the management of classified information

Language

English – Upper Intermediate/Advanced

Desirable Qualifications

Ø Knowledge of NATO security policies, procedures and contributing organizations

Ø Experience with the application of security to in all disciplines (Personnel, Physical, Security of Information, and CIS)

Ø Experience with the conduct of security audits and compliance audits

Ø Experience with the development of curriculum and execution of educational activities and trainings

Personal Attributes/Competencies

The ideal candidate will demonstrate professional communication skills, with the ability to clearly and diplomatically convey complex security information. They must be capable of working effectively with personnel of all ranks, roles, and statuses across a multinational environment. Integrity, discretion, and sound judgement are required in handling sensitive or classified information. The candidate should also exhibit adaptability and resilience when responding to evolving security challenges while maintaining NATO standards and fostering trust among stakeholders.

Work Environment

The work is normally performed in an office environment.

NOTE: The work both oral and written in this post and in this headquarters as a whole is conducted mainly in English.

Travel on temporary duty may be required for several conferences.

Irregular working hours may be required, especially during exercises/events.

How To Apply For a NATO Civilian post at JWC:

JWC, as an equal opportunities employer, values diverse backgrounds and perspectives and is committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and talented workforce. We welcome applications from nationals of all NATO Member States and strongly encourage women to apply.

Applications are to be submitted, in English, using the NATO Talent Acquisition Platform (NTAP) (https://nato.taleo.net/careersection/2/jobsearch.ftl?lang-en). Applications submitted by other means will not be accepted.

NTAP allows for the adding of attachments. Candidates are to attach a copy of the qualification(s)/certificate(s) covering the highest level of relevant education and vocational qualifications held to support their application.

Applications are automatically acknowledged within one working day after submission. In the absence of an acknowledgement please make sure the submission process is completed or re-submit the application. Applications will not be accepted after the deadline.

All applications prepared, in whole or in part, by means of such generative or creative AI applications may be rejected without further consideration at NATO’s sole discretion, and NATO reserves the right to take further steps in such cases as appropriate.

Notes for NATO Civilian Human Resources Managers: if you have qualified redundant staff at grade G15/A-2, who wish to be considered for this post, please advise JWC Civilian HR no later than the closing date.

Contract:

The successful applicant will be offered a three-year definite duration employment contract after which a further contract may be offered. Serving staff will be offered a contract in accordance with the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations.

Starting basic salary is NOK 93,933.00 per month (tax-free). Additional allowances may apply depending on the personal circumstances of the successful candidate. For further details see NATO Terms & Conditions.

7) Lead the Joint enabling part of the nations DPCS analysis, in the provision of ACO contribution to the countries impact analysis;

9) Lead the Joint Enabling Domain part of the Bi-SC Suitability and Risk Assessment;
10) Support Force generation and verification with NDPP step 5 analytical data in the relevant domain expertise;

Our organisation
Joint Force Command Brunssum (JFCBS) provides a Joint headquarters to plan, prepare and conduct operations to support NATO’s core tasks, at the Joint Operational level, as directed by SACEUR. The incumbent's duties are:

- Manages directly the daily operations related to the HQ SACT finance and accounting team.

title: Staff Officer (Wargame Designer/Support Officer) - Project Linked NIC
description:
Staff Officer (Wargame Designer/Support Officer) – Project Linked NATO International Civilian

If you are an experienced Staff Officer (Wargame Designer/Support Officer) looking to join a dynamic team working in a multi-national environment, JFTC would be interested in hearing from you!

Post Context:

The Joint Force Training Centre supports Warfare Development, contributing to concept development and maintenance of joint doctrine and standards while coordinating the integration of experimentation, capability development, and interoperability to improve NATO’s interoperability, capabilities, and operational effectiveness.

The Training and Exercise Enabling Division (TEED) enables training and exercises, and warfare development events. Likewise, the Division provides the basis for the Joint Force Training Centre’s engagement with Allied Command Transformation Doctrine validation activities. The Division also maintains the JFTC’s analysis and lessons learned capability for both training/exercise/experimentation and institutional improvement.

The Concepts, Capability Integration & Experimentation (CCIE) Branch provides resources to ensure JFTC’s warfare development through doctrine validation and support to the CD&E methodology.

This position is required to provide JFTC with professional military wargaming expertise in support of NATO 2030, NATO Wargaming Capability, future training and exercise development, Multi-Domain Operations (MDO), Digital Transformation, the Future Exercise Model and Future Modelling & Simulation. The incumbent will design, develop, facilitate, analyze and report professional wargames that support joint, combined and multinational headquarters in testing plans, exploring options, supporting alternative analysis and improving decision-making.

The incumbent acts as JFTC’s subject matter expert for professional military wargame design in support of NATO 2030, NATO Wargaming Capability, future training and exercise development, and warfare development. The post supports joint, combined and multinational headquarters by translating operational and tactical problems into professional wargaming activities and decision-support outputs, integrating multi-domain considerations and relevant analytical tools where appropriate.

Reports to: Branch Head (Concepts, Cap Integration & Exp) - OF-4

Principal Duties:

The Staff Officer Wargame Designer is responsible for the design, development, facilitation, adjudication, analysis and reporting of professional military wargames. Duties include:

a. Designs professional military wargames supporting operational and tactical-level training, planning, experimentation and decision-making.

b. Translates operational and tactical problems into wargame objectives, scenarios, player roles, decision points, adjudication methods, data-capture plans and analytical outputs.

c. Develops wargame concepts, mechanics, scenario material, force laydowns, injects, adjudication rules, assessment criteria and supporting documentation.

d. Integrates relevant operational context, regional plans, real-world considerations and multi-domain factors, including land, air, maritime, space, cyber, sustainment, information and special operations, into wargame design and execution.

e. Leads or supports multidisciplinary teams, applies qualitative and quantitative analysis methods, and produces reports, briefings, decision-support products, recommendations and lessons.

Decision Authority - Authorized to adjust day-to-day work priorities for assigned personnel and contributors to meet approved wargaming activity, project or programme requirements.

Special Requirements and Additional Duties:

Lessons Learned (LL) is an integrated part of all activities. LL requests, planning, creation, collection, staffing and handling in accordance with the NATO LL Process as an integrated part of any activity.

The employee may be required to perform a similar range of duties elsewhere within the organisation at the same grade without there being any change to the contract

a. Flexibility Clause: In order for the command to deal with emergent requirements the incumbent may be required to perform other related duties as directed (in particular, the incumbent can expect to work as a member of Working Groups, Project Teams, etc. for defined periods of time).

b. Annual TDY Requirement: The incumbent may be required to undertake Temporary Duty (TDY) and/or travel within and outside NATO’s boundaries for up to 65 days per year.

Personnel are expected to conduct themselves in accordance with the current NATO Code of Conduct agreed by the North Atlantic Council (NAC), and thus display the core values of integrity, impartiality, loyalty, accountability, and professionalism.

The work is normally performed in a Normal NATO office working environment.

Normal Working Conditions apply.

The risk of injury is categorised as No Risk.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Experience:

1) Minimum 3 years’ experience designing, developing, facilitating, evaluating or supporting professional military wargames, preferably for joint, combined or multinational headquarters.

2) Experience translating operational or tactical problems into wargame objectives, scenarios, player guidance, decision points, adjudication methods, data-capture plans and analytical outputs.

3) Experience supporting or conducting joint operational planning at tactical, operational or strategic level, preferably in a NATO, national military, multinational or defence-related environment.

4) Experience conducting or supporting seminars, tabletop exercises, command post exercises, analytical wargames or similar military decision-support activities, including alternative analysis, operational analysis, operations assessment, lessons learned or other structured decision-support methodologies.

5) Strong facilitation, briefing, stakeholder engagement and report-writing skills, including experience working in a multinational environment and presenting complex information to senior military or civilian decision-makers.

6) University Degree in military science, defence studies, strategic planning, systems analysis, operations research, statistics, computer-assisted modelling or a related discipline or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training.

Education/Training:

University Degree and 2 years function related experience, or Higher Secondary education and completed advanced vocational training leading to a professional qualification or professional accreditation with 4 years post related experience.

Language:

English - SLP 3333 - (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing)

NOTE: The work both oral and written in this post and in this Headquarters as a whole is conducted mainly in English.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Experience:

1) Significant military or defence experience, including operational-level joint, combined or multinational planning appointments, and experience working with senior military/civilian leaders or multinational partners.

2) Experience with NATO or equivalent exercise planning processes, operational art, campaign design, force employment and military decision-making processes.

3) Experience with modelling and simulation tools, constructive simulation databases, computer-assisted exercises, professional wargaming software, AI-assisted wargaming, data analytics or decision-support systems.

4) Knowledge of operational analysis, alternative analysis, operations assessment or structured analytical methodologies, and/or experience with academia, industry, think tanks or defence research organizations.

Education/Training:

1) NATO, national, commercial or equivalent training in wargaming, strategic/operational planning, alternative analysis, operations assessment, operational analysis, data analytics, decision-support methods, modelling and simulation, AI-enabled analytical tools or project/programme management.

2) Senior-level Joint Command and Staff College, NATO Defence College, national equivalent or comparable senior professional military education.

3) Master’s degree in military science, defence studies, strategic planning, systems analysis, operations research, statistics, computer-assisted modelling or a related discipline.

4) To meet the organizational requirements, the incumbent attends training courses/seminars to maintain or achieve functional qualifications in the subject field of service.

5) Course: ETE-WG-36888 - NATO Wargaming Practitioner Course.
